answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded random walks, limiting how far influence can diffuse from its sources. A sybil cluster with few links to the honest network forms a sparse external cut and therefore has low conductance; under degree and walk-length assumptions, its probability of receiving trusted mass—and thus its aggregate voting weight—is bounded by that bottleneck. The walnut-and-cedar fable is only an analogy: the guarantee comes from the graph’s measured cuts, not its labels.
